document.abstract: A workflow is generally defined as “a system for managing repetitive processes and tasks that occur in a particular order.” I tend to conceptualize workflows with a diagram showing applied products and signal flows and then describe the processes and action steps in a list as a first concept that, when put into practice, is modified with additional customizations according to the implementer's needs or even personal preferences. Each one may be different in concept versus in implementation. First concepts are bound to be modified, although the initial designs of workflows are particularly important so that collaboration can begin to form into a working template that will likely continue to develop throughout its implementation.
